progressionAssessment.rationale: Python and discrete mathematics precede algorithms, followed by advanced algorithms and C++ and Haskell development. Mathematical methods and linear algebra support numerical methods, signals and advanced calculus. Introductory data analysis precedes machine learning and deep learning.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The direct interests support one computing response across systems, algorithms, software and mathematical methods. A data and AI emphasis is already represented within it. A second option would reuse most of the same technical curriculum or shift into other fields without an independently supported programme-level direction.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both cover formal logic. The UCR course also teaches discrete mathematics.
Both develop algorithm and data-structure design and analysis. Groningen teaches these in C.
Both study advanced algorithm design and analysis. UCR includes algebraic algorithms, optimisation and network flows.
Both teach basic programming and problem solving. UCR uses Python. Groningen uses other languages in its sequence.
Both cover differentiation, integration and differential equations.
Both study vectors, matrices and linear transformations.
Both develop multivariable calculus. UCR also covers differential equations.
Both cover probability distributions and statistical inference.
Several UCR courses introduce parts of computing. None surveys the discipline and its research as a whole.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics spans both areas and appears alongside the separate Groningen Logic course.
Both study how operating systems manage processes, memory and storage. UCR also covers computer networks.
Both teach relational databases and query languages. Groningen develops a broader information-systems foundation.
Both develop software design and testing skills. UCR works in C++ and Haskell. Groningen requires a larger team project.
Networks & Operating Systems includes systems concepts. Groningen has a separate course on computer architecture and machine organisation.
Introduction to Programming and Software Development include object-oriented programming. They appear alongside other components in the table.
The combined UCR Networks & Operating Systems course includes networking and appears alongside Operating Systems.
UCR Software Development includes C++ and Haskell. Groningen has a separate advanced programming course.
Software Development uses Haskell and appears alongside Software Engineering. Groningen has a separate functional programming course.
The UCR selection has programming, databases and networking. It lacks a dedicated course in web engineering.
UCR logic and programming are relevant foundations. Groningen has a separate course in automata and formal languages.
UCR studies aspects of privacy and database access. Groningen requires a separate technical information security course.
UCR covers network protocols and operating-system concepts. Groningen teaches distributed systems as a separate subject.
The Groningen project is required. UCR’s optional independent research appears separately.
This is approved elective space. It does not correspond to a single course.
Both teach machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
UCR computer vision interprets images. Groningen teaches graphics rendering and visualisation.
UCR courses develop general research skills and computing project work. Groningen has a dedicated research preparation course.

notes.text: UCR combines substantial computing with a broader liberal arts and sciences curriculum. Groningen requires separate courses in computer architecture, web engineering, security and distributed systems, and a bachelor’s project.

audience.programmeDescription: Computing Science at the University of Groningen studies how software and computer systems work and how to design them. It combines programming and algorithms with mathematics, systems and a required research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option concentrates on software, algorithms and systems, with applications in data science and machine learning.

componentNotes.y3-free-minor: Students can use this space for eligible electives, a minor or an approved study period. An internship can use part of the 30 EC.
componentNotes.y3-bachelor-project: The project follows the first-year curriculum and at least 75 EC from years two and three.
